moduleTitle: Performing Data-driven Testing using Excel Files
learningObjectives: Explain the process for importing data from an Excel file into a test within Testim, ensuring effective data management.
Demonstrate how to run a test using parameterized variables to validate different outputs across multiple data sets.

elements.description: The Setup-step Excel/CSV workflow uses the first row for parameter names, then subsequent data rows for individual data sets, with a documented 1200-row limit. Test data must fit the documented 2 MB limit. The separate reusable Test Data library supports CSV, JSON and Excel; do not conflate that resource workflow with embedded Setup data.
A single file can define multiple ordered data sets, letting one test run repeatedly against a whole matrix of input combinations instead of a single hardcoded scenario.

elements.text: Column headers name parameters; data rows supply their values. Uploaded data is a snapshot: changing the local file requires re-upload, while an external-source configuration can parse its source on each run.

bulletPoints: Excel/CSV Setup upload: header row names parameters; subsequent rows provide data sets.
Observe the documented row/size limits and inspect parsed values.
Upload is a snapshot; external-source configuration can load data on each run.
Reusable Resource data files are distinct from embedded Setup data.
Review/remove unwanted old embedded data explicitly rather than assuming automatic cleanup.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: Config File vs. Params File for data-driven CLI runs

elements.description: A Config File can override the Visual Editor's test data at either the execution level or a specific test level (via overrideTestData) — and it's also how an external data source (like a linked CSV file, or a database) is supplied instead of an uploaded file.

A params file supplies execution-wide parameter values. JSON is supported; current documentation also supports JavaScript/module.exports. Config hooks with overrideTestData can target named tests. Verify precedence, including the separate reusable-file Prioritize test data option, instead of assuming every source always overrides every other.

bulletPoints: Config File: overrides test data at execution level OR a specific test (overrideTestData); also links external sources (CSV, database).
Params files support JSON or JavaScript/module.exports and execution-wide scope.
Both require running via the CLI, not the Visual Editor.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: Where the multiple data sets actually run

elements.description: For the documented embedded Setup data workflow, ordinary editor playback runs the first data set. CLI, Scheduler or local suite execution can run the ordered data sets; inspect each data-set result. This is scoped to that workflow, not certification that every newer reusable-file option has identical playback behavior.

elements.text: This is a common trap: seeing a single successful editor run and assuming the whole data set matrix has been exercised, when only row one has actually been used.

bulletPoints: Editor run = first data set only.
CLI / Scheduler / local suite run = every data set, in order.

examPitfalls.title: Assuming an editor run exercises every row of the uploaded data
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Uploading a 10-row Excel file, clicking Play in the editor once, and concluding all 10 data combinations were tested.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: For embedded Setup data, use CLI, Scheduler or local suite execution to cover multiple data sets and inspect their results. Include a header row separately from the intended data-row count.

practiceQuiz.scenario: In the documented Setup-step Excel/CSV upload, how do rows after the parameter-name header map to data sets?

options.text: The whole file becomes a single data set.
Each subsequent data row defines a data set, subject to the documented 1200-row limit.
Each column becomes a separate test.
Only the first row is ever used, regardless of run method.

practiceQuiz.hint: The header names parameters; subsequent rows supply their values.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The first row supplies parameter names; subsequent rows define individual sets of values. Columns are parameters, not separate tests.

optionExplanations.A: The data rows supply separate sets rather than one whole-file set.
optionExplanations.B: Rows after the header define sets of parameter values.
optionExplanations.C: Headers name parameters, not separate tests.
optionExplanations.D: Supported multi-set runners can execute subsequent sets.

practiceQuiz.scenario: An embedded Setup data upload has one header row and five data rows. An ordinary editor playback passes. Under the documented workflow, how many data sets did that playback run?

options.text: All 5.
Only the first data set.
None — Excel files aren't usable from the editor.
A random data set is chosen each run.

practiceQuiz.hint: The editor run has a well-known limitation here.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Ordinary editor playback for embedded Setup data runs the first set. The header is not a sixth data set; inspect CLI/Scheduler/local-suite results to confirm broader coverage.

optionExplanations.A: Ordinary embedded-Setup editor playback does not cover all five sets.
optionExplanations.B: The documented ordinary editor playback uses the first set.
optionExplanations.C: Embedded Excel/CSV data is usable in the editor.
optionExplanations.D: The documented workflow uses the first set rather than choosing randomly.

practiceQuiz.scenario: According to Testim's official documentation, what happens to test data already added to a test's Setup step when you upload a new data set?

options.text: It's automatically removed and replaced.
It stays in the test until it's explicitly removed.
It's silently merged with the old data, doubling the rows.
The test becomes locked and uneditable.

practiceQuiz.hint: Nothing is cleaned up automatically here.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The embedded data documentation says previous data is not automatically removed until explicitly removed. Inspect the effective data instead of assuming upload proves cleanup. Reusable-file replacement/prioritization is a distinct resource workflow.

optionExplanations.A: The source says previous embedded data is not automatically removed.
optionExplanations.B: Review and remove unwanted old embedded data explicitly.
optionExplanations.C: The source does not promise automatic row doubling on every upload.
optionExplanations.D: Adding data does not document a locked/uneditable test.

practiceQuiz.scenario: What's the key difference between a Params File and a Config File when supplying data-driven test data via the CLI?

options.text: A Params File only works with the Visual Editor, never the CLI.
A Config File applies its overrides execution-wide only; a Params File is scoped to one specific test.
Params files supply execution-wide values, while config hooks can target named tests with overrideTestData.
Both apply only to a single, specifically named test.

practiceQuiz.hint: One of them can target a single test; the other can't.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Params-file scope covers tests in one execution; config hooks can supply execution-wide values or per-test overrideTestData. Current params-file documentation supports JSON and JavaScript exports; reusable file priority is a separate mechanism.

optionExplanations.A: Params files are used by CLI execution.
optionExplanations.B: This reverses named-test config scope versus execution-wide params-file scope.
optionExplanations.C: Config hooks can target tests, while params files supply execution-wide values.
optionExplanations.D: Both are not restricted to one named test.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Besides the embedded Setup upload, which documented approach can load CSV/database data for data-driven runs?

options.text: A live Slack channel feed.
An external source, such as a CSV file or a database, linked via a Config File.
A Google Calendar event.
A Chrome bookmark folder.

practiceQuiz.hint: The Config File can link to data instead of embedding it.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Configuration hooks can load external data and pass objects to applicable tests. A source is loaded by the configured code, not magically linked by file upload alone.

optionExplanations.A: This is not the stated documented external-data workflow.
optionExplanations.B: Config hooks can load the supported external source into data objects.
optionExplanations.C: Calendar scheduling does not supply this test dataset.
optionExplanations.D: Browser bookmarks are not this external-data mechanism.

quickRecap.value: Setup upload documents Excel/CSV; reusable Resources support CSV/JSON/Excel. Observe the 2 MB limit.
Header names parameters; subsequent rows supply data sets, with the documented 1200-row limit.
Ordinary embedded-Setup playback uses the first data set.
Executes every data set, in order.
Not auto-removed — stays until explicitly deleted.
Config hooks can target named tests; JSON/JS params files supply execution-wide values. Check separate reusable-file priority.
